label: D2 after choosing a2 and landing in S1 (rare a2->S1 transition)
explanation: Fires at D2 when the agent chose a2 and the observed state is S1, i.e. a rare a2->S1 transition; 96% of activation mass is at such steps, and the unit never fires at GO, almost never after a1 or in S2. Uses only current inputs (in_action, in_state). Strongest when the agent is committed to a2 (repeated a2 choices, S2 good, strongly negative choice logit); false positives are mostly a2->S1 steps right after a switch from a1 or in a1-dominated histories (adding stay==1 raises precision to 0.92 but lowers recall to 0.68). A weak residual (~4% mass) fires at D1 with reward 1 during long runs of rewarded a2 choices.

issues: The core claim holds. GO never fires (0 of 380619 steps). D2 after a1 has precision 0.0001 and D2 in S2 has precision 0.0003. D2 holds 96.2% of the activation mass. Reported test scores reproduce: P 0.851, R 0.824, F1 0.837, mass recall 0.963.

There is one systematic false-positive class: an a2->S1 step on a trial right after an a1 trial (a switch from a1). Here the unit is almost silent. Dev precision for that subset is 0.052 (3349 predicted steps), so the subset alone accounts for about 40% of all dev false positives. When the previous trial was a2, precision is 0.918. On the window's first trial (prev_action unknown) it is 0.903. The explanation mentions switch-from-a1 false positives, but the label and predicate do not exclude them.

The explanation's reason for keeping the simpler predicate is misleading. stay==1 cut recall to 0.68 because stay is -1 (unknown) on each window's first trial, not because the unit needs repeated choices. Excluding only switches, with prev_action != 1, keeps recall and raises test precision: P 0.908, R 0.821, F1 0.862, mass recall 0.962.

The leftover false positives fall where S1 is good (dev precision 0.64 when good==1, against 0.93 when good==2). This fits the 'committed to a2 / S2 good' description. The leftover misses are weak D1 activations (r1 during a2 runs, 3.7% of mass, mostly in the bottom activation quartile). These are acceptable leftovers. Adding a D1 term for them drops test F1 to 0.66.
